gen-dafont-true-north-gf-hanuman: True North packs its lowercase into a tall middle band, so lines look stocky, and its curves refuse to close. Hanuman, a text serif with a high-waisted lowercase, loosens things with wide-set terminals on its s.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-kadwa: True North is all stocky, tall-middled bold, with curves that refuse to close. Kadwa, a serif with open-ended curves and a large x-height, can be sized down a notch without losing its footing.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-noticia-text: Literary and dignified, Noticia Text greets each curve with a big visible entrance. Noticia Text does the steady reading, while True North does the shouting, with stocky tall-middled letters and curves left open.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-piazzolla: True North hits hard: stocky, bold, with curves left ajar. Piazzolla, a classic serif whose lowercase nearly matches its capitals, reads with refined authority over a full page of text.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-pridi: True North's tall middle band makes every line look stocky. What ties them is shared stature: Pridi's small letters stand almost capital-sized, with generous space between curve ends and stems.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-scope-one: Chunky and a bit stubborn, True North sets its curves ajar and its middle band tall. And Scope One, a text serif whose counters spill outward beside stubby ascenders, reads with a sturdy, grounded ease.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-slabo-13px: True North arrives stocky and bold, its curves refusing to close. Headlines are where True North hits hardest, while Slabo 13px, a serif with large open counters, keeps rounded letters clear.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-suwannaphum: Curves that refuse to close give True North its stubborn look. Suwannaphum, a classic serif, matches that sturdy stance with a c bent open like a paperclip and a high, squared-off x-height.
gen-dafont-true-north-manrope: True North stands stocky, its curves stubbornly refusing to close. Manrope, a sans drawn with a steady rolling-ball line, leaves a bright gap at each curve's mouth, so paragraphs glide along comfortably.
gen-dafont-true-north-roboto-slab: Curves that refuse to close and a middle band so tall the lines look stocky: that is True North. Roboto Slab, a slab-serif with open throats, keeps the structure tidy underneath.
